clue.text: Estates will not seem unusual here?

definitions.text: Estates will not seem unusual here?

indicators.note: unusual tells us the letters of these three words are set out in a new order

explanation.surface: A remark that housing developments look perfectly ordinary in a certain kind of place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unusual' rearranges ESTATES WILL NOT; the whole clue then defines: satellite towns are built of housing estates, so estates look normal there.
explanation.definitionFit: Satellite towns are smaller settlements built around a city, largely made up of housing estates, so estates are the norm there.

clue.text: Design a cute oval pressure cooker

indicators.note: to design is to arrange afresh, so the letters of the following words are laid out anew

explanation.surface: Someone designs a pretty oval-shaped pressure cooker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Design' poses as a verb about making a cooker, but it is the anagram signal; the article already stands where the answer begins, so only the two words after it are reordered.
explanation.definitionFit: An autoclave is a strong sealed vessel that heats under pressure, used for sterilising or cooking.

clue.text: No good stocking this antelope in part of UK

indicators.note: NG stocking (held inside) the antelope makes the region, so taking those letters out of the region leaves the antelope

parts.note: England is one of the countries of the United Kingdom

explanation.surface: A region of Britain has no use for keeping a particular antelope.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as: NG stocking this antelope gives a part of the UK, so E(NG)LAND with NG removed leaves the antelope.
explanation.definitionFit: The eland is a large African antelope with spiralled horns.

clue.text: Make picturesque exotic places entertaining also

indicators.note: entertaining in its sense of hosting or holding, so one piece takes in another
exotic suggests something strange or altered, so the letters of places are mixed up

parts.note: also and and both add something further

explanation.surface: Faraway places that are also fun to visit look picturesque.
explanation.walkthrough: 'exotic' gives LSCAPE; 'entertaining' (hosting) houses the second piece after its first letter. 'Make picturesque' is a verb: to landscape a garden.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb, to landscape is to lay out grounds attractively with planting and contours, making them prettier.

clue.text: Unusual act it's silent

indicators.note: unusual signals that the letters that follow are set out differently

parts.note: the word it, with the 's read as a link meaning is

explanation.surface: A strange performance in which nobody speaks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unusual' rearranges ACT IT; the 's is read as 'is', linking wordplay to definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Tacit means unspoken, understood or implied without being said aloud.

clue.text: Try to have the last word with this, primarily

definitions.text: Try to have the last word with this, primarily

parts.note: to try something is to test it
amen is the word said at the end of a prayer

indicators.note: primarily points to the first letter of the word this

explanation.surface: An invitation to get the final say by using a certain document.
explanation.walkthrough: TEST + AMEN + T (first of 'this'); the whole clue defines, since a will lets the dead have the final say.
explanation.definitionFit: A last will and testament is the legal document by which a person's wishes are carried out after death.

clue.text: Row rather encapsulates it

indicators.note: encapsulates tells us the answer is held inside the run of letters of Row rather

explanation.surface: A quarrel is the best summary of a certain emotion.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters sit inside 'roW RATHer'; a row is a fit of anger, so the clue as a whole also describes the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Wrath is intense anger, the feeling that fuels a furious row.

clue.text: Raise mischief with flier

explanation.surface: Someone stirs up trouble with an aviator.
explanation.definitionFit: To skylark is to frolic and play pranks; a skylark is also a songbird famous for singing in flight.

clue.text: Banks almost all gone from altering sea-level

indicators.note: altering signals the remaining letters change their order
gone from shows those letters leave the word sea-level
almost means all is cut short by its final letter

explanation.surface: Riverbanks have nearly vanished because sea levels are changing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost all' gives AL; 'gone from' removes it from SEALEVEL, leaving SEEVEL, which 'altering' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: Levees are raised embankments along a river that hold back floodwater.

clue.text: Next raise includes bonus

indicators.note: includes shows the answer is held within the letters of Next raise

explanation.surface: An upcoming pay rise comes with a bonus.
explanation.definitionFit: An extra is something additional, over and above what is expected, like a bonus.

clue.text: Scary scene's missing chapter badly needed

indicators.note: badly signals the remaining letters are jumbled
missing means the letter for chapter is left out

parts.note: the word scene, its 's read as is

explanation.surface: A frightening scene in a film is cut and its absence is keenly felt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'missing' takes C from SCARYSCENE, leaving SARYSCENE, which 'badly' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: Necessary means essential or required, just as something needed is.

clue.text: Having doubled radius, repeats ciphers

indicators.note: a radius doubled is a diameter, so the letter for radius is swapped for the letter for diameter

parts.note: encores are performances repeated at the audience's call

explanation.surface: A geometry problem where a circle's radius is doubled and a pattern repeats.
explanation.walkthrough: R (radius) doubled becomes D (diameter): ENCORES with its R changed to D.
explanation.definitionFit: To encode a message is to put it into secret code, which is what ciphering it means.

clue.text: Skill in reversing inhibits pain in the neck, to some extent

definitions.text: in the neck, to some extent

indicators.note: inhibits in the sense of holding in, so one piece contains another
in reversing tells us the word for skill is turned round

parts.note: art is skill, as in the art of conversation
an ache is a dull pain

explanation.surface: A clever reversal in a hold stops a pain in the neck.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in reversing' gives TRA. 'pain in the neck' looks like one phrase, but only 'pain' is wordplay; the windpipe is only partly in the neck, hence 'to some extent'.
explanation.definitionFit: The windpipe runs down from the larynx partly through the throat and into the chest, so it lies partly within the neck.

clue.text: It's found in barrels, and around bars

explanation.surface: Something is located in casks and also near pubs.
explanation.definitionFit: A stave is one of the curved wooden strips forming a barrel's side; it is also the musical staff on which bars of music are written.

clue.text: Immoderate French are involved in kinky sex and vice

indicators.note: involved in shows one piece is wrapped inside another
kinky, meaning twisted, signals the letters are rearranged

parts.note: es is the French for are, as in tu es

explanation.surface: French people are implicated in a scandal of perverse sex and vice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'kinky' gives EXCSIVE; 'involved in' places the French word inside it. French 'es' is the form of 'are' used with 'tu'.
explanation.definitionFit: Excessive means going beyond reasonable limits, which is what immoderate also means.

clue.text: Drink's a temptation once it gives you a lift

parts.note: the apple was the fruit Eve was tempted by in Eden
a jack is a device for lifting a car

explanation.surface: Alcohol was once a lure because it raises your spirits.
explanation.walkthrough: APPLE (the Eden temptation) + JACK (a car lifter).
explanation.definitionFit: Applejack is an American brandy distilled from cider.

clue.text: Hope stats get updated soon

indicators.note: get updated signals that the letters are revised into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone hopes the figures will be refreshed quickly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'get updated' rearranges HOPE STATS.
explanation.definitionFit: Posthaste means with all possible speed, so at the earliest moment.

clue.text: One suggestion for a starter

parts.note: an is the indefinite article, meaning one
a tip is a useful suggestion
as to means for or concerning

explanation.surface: A single idea for how to begin a meal.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads as one idea for a meal's first course, but splits into three pieces; 'as to' is a phrase meaning regarding.
explanation.definitionFit: Antipasto is the Italian first course of cold meats and vegetables served before the main dish.

clue.text: Half-hearted soccer refs teased by graffiti artists?

indicators.note: teased, as in teased out or combed, signals the letters are rearranged
the heart of the word soccer is its double letter, and half of it goes

explanation.surface: Vandals with spray cans mock referees at a lacklustre football match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Half-hearted' drops one of the middle Cs of SOCCER; 'teased' rearranges SOCER REFS. The question mark flags a loose definition: wall painters in a playful sense.
explanation.definitionFit: A fresco is a painting made on a wall, so wall painters are jokingly likened to graffiti artists.

clue.text: Instigates putting warning in papers

indicators.note: in shows one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: FTs, plural of FT, the Financial Times newspaper
an omen is a warning of what is to come

explanation.surface: Someone stirs things up by printing a warning in the newspapers.
explanation.walkthrough: FT is the Financial Times, the paper this puzzle appears in, so 'papers' is its plural.
explanation.definitionFit: To foment trouble is to stir it up or provoke it.

clue.text: Excise number: one tenth, possibly

parts.note: a levy whose rate is traditionally a tenth of produce or income, paid to the church

explanation.definitionFit: A tithe is a tax or contribution of a tenth of one's earnings, historically paid to support the church.

clue.text: Eastern rallies boosted credit

indicators.note: in a down entry boosted means pushed upwards, so the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: rallies and meets are both gatherings

explanation.surface: Eastern share prices rally and boost credit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'boosted' in a down answer lifts the word up the grid, making STEEM; 'rallies' poses as a market rise.
explanation.definitionFit: To give someone credit is to show them respect or high regard.

clue.text: Dislike exclusive group's attitude

parts.note: to mind something is to object to or dislike it
a set is an exclusive social group, as in the jet set; the 's is a link

explanation.surface: A snobbish clique's attitude is resented.
explanation.definitionFit: A mindset is a fixed way of thinking, an outlook or attitude.

clue.text: Relating to feature space agency put at centre of satellite

parts.note: NASA is the American space agency

indicators.note: centre of picks the middle letter of the word satellite

explanation.surface: Space agency staff fix a part at the heart of a satellite.
explanation.walkthrough: NASA + L, the middle letter of 'satellite'. The 'feature' is a facial feature, the nose.
explanation.definitionFit: Nasal means having to do with the nose, the facial feature in the middle of the face.

clue.text: Idiot has lost article in Belgian city

indicators.note: has lost signals the article is removed

parts.note: Antwerp is a port city in Belgium
an is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A fool mislaid an item in a city in Belgium.
explanation.walkthrough: 'has lost' takes AN from ANTWERP.
explanation.definitionFit: A twerp is a silly or foolish person.

clue.text: Give warning about short measure in nightclub

indicators.note: about shows the first piece goes round the second

parts.note: to hoot is to sound a horn as a warning
tsp is the short form of teaspoon, a kitchen measure

explanation.surface: Someone complains about being served short measures in a nightclub.
explanation.walkthrough: TSP inside HOOT. 'short measure' looks like a complaint about drinks, but it is an abbreviated measure.
explanation.definitionFit: A hot spot is a lively, popular venue for entertainment, such as a club.

clue.text: Transport system makes tidy return

indicators.note: return signals that the word is turned back to front

parts.note: to smart up something is to make it neat and tidy

explanation.surface: A transport network makes a tidy profit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'return' turns SMART round. 'return' poses as a financial return.
explanation.definitionFit: Trams, streetcars running on rails in city streets, form a public transport network.

clue.text: It could produce sensations devoid of love

definitions.text: It could produce sensations devoid of love

indicators.note: could produce signals the remaining letters can be made into something new
devoid of means without, so that letter is dropped

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, written as the letter O

explanation.surface: A remark that some behaviour leaves people feeling unloved.
explanation.walkthrough: 'devoid of' drops O (love) from SENSATIONS, and 'could produce' rearranges the rest; the whole clue also describes the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Spite and unkindness make people feel unloved, creating cold, loveless feelings.

clue.text: Part of supermarket is flanked by drink

indicators.note: flanked by means having something on each side, so one piece sits within the other

parts.note: ale is a type of beer

explanation.surface: Part of a supermarket sits between shelves of drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drink' sits on both sides of the short word, a common way for 'flanked by' to work.
explanation.definitionFit: An aisle is a passage between rows of shelves in a shop.

clue.text: Cartesian sum?

parts.note: Descartes' cogito ergo sum, where sum is Latin for I am, a statement of one's own being

explanation.definitionFit: Descartes' sum, meaning I am, is a declaration of one's own existence, an assertion of identity.
